name: Lower third training routine

card.summary: A lower third training routine is a combined set of jaw, neck and posture habits plus leanness aimed at a more defined jawline and lower face.
card.note: Chewing-based jaw training can enlarge the masseter and has been linked to jaw discomfort in some people.

quick.overview:
The lower third of the face covers the jaw, chin and neck. A lower third routine bundles several habits that practitioners use to sharpen it: chewing exercises, neck training, tongue and breathing posture, and staying lean.

The appearance chain is stated plainly by users: stronger chewing muscles and a thicker neck add visible width and definition, while lower body fat reveals the jaw outline. A looksmax.org post shows one such routine with before-and-after photos, though the poster notes puberty and fat loss also played a part.
quick.how: A routine shared on looksmax.org lists daily sessions with a resistance chewing device, hardened sugar-free gum chewed for a few hours a day, neck exercises twice a week, attention to tongue posture, nose breathing and back sleeping, and a low-carbohydrate diet to stay at low body fat with high water intake.
quick.risks: The masseter muscle can enlarge with habitual gum chewing or clenching, and this enlargement may be asymmetric and sometimes coincides with jaw joint problems. Effects of the combined routine have not been trialled.

lead: The lower third training routine is a looksmaxxing term for a personal programme targeting the lower part of the face: the jaw, chin, neck and submental area. It combines muscle training, posture habits and diet, with the aim of a more defined jawline and a stronger-looking neck.[1]

A routine posted on looksmax.org illustrates the format. It includes two daily sessions of about fifteen minutes with a resistance chewing device, long daily periods of chewing hardened sugar-free gum, neck training twice weekly, "hard mewing" tongue posture, correct swallowing, nose breathing and sleeping on the back. The poster also described staying around single-digit body fat through low carbohydrates and high water intake.[1] Replies and the poster's own photos note that puberty and fat loss may account for part of the change.[1]

The masseter, the main chewing muscle, can grow with repeated heavy use. Medical references note that enlargement occurs in people who clench or grind their teeth and in those who habitually chew gum, and that it can alter facial shape.[2] No clinical trials have tested the full routine.

chain: Add muscle volume at the jaw and neck
Lower body fat shows the outline
angle.text: Practitioners combine muscle work and leanness to enlarge and reveal the jaw and neck. The masseter can enlarge with chewing, and lower body fat makes the contour more visible.

paras: The routine is not a single standardised programme; each person's version differs. A common template has four parts: chewing work, neck training, ongoing posture checks and nutrition.[1]
The shared routine uses a resistance jaw trainer twice daily and chews hardened gum for hours across the day. The poster says various branded and generic trainers felt the same to him.[1]
Neck exercises are done twice weekly in the example given; details were hidden behind spoilers in the post.[1]
Items watched include tongue position (mewing), holding posture, swallowing technique, nasal breathing and sleeping on the back.[1]
The poster avoids carbohydrates to stay lean, drinks several litres of water daily and replaces electrolytes.[1]
Masseter enlargement is documented in habitual gum chewers and people with bruxism; it may be uneven and can coincide with temporomandibular joint problems.[2]

lore.intro: Users post personal routines with photos, framing the lower third as the part of the face that responds to training.[1]

claims.claim: Chewing and neck work, plus leanness, sharpen the jaw and lower face
claims.believers: The poster shared before and after images and credits the routine, while acknowledging puberty and fat loss as contributors.[1]
claims.experts: Medical references report that chewing gum habitually and clenching can enlarge the masseter; the combined routine has not been studied.[2]
